shapes.text: The Cable Effects Study Missions

shapes.name: Rectangle 2
shapes.text: Do electrical cable harnesses significantly affect dynamics of precision spacecraft structures?Lightweight and with stringent jitter budgetsCable harnesses are generally not included in spacecraft structural design.  As a consequence:Models and designs are overly conservativeIsolation system requirements are too stringentStructural control systems may be adversely affected by plant model errorsMotivation: develop techniques and methodologies to incorporate cable dynamics in models thereby reducing conservatism and program risk

shapes.name: Title 1
shapes.text: The Why of theCable Effects Study

shapes.name: Content Placeholder 2
shapes.text: Cable harnesses are a large part of spacecraft mass and generally considered a non-structural component at low frequencies. A survey showed that the cable-to-structure mass ratio for DoD and commercial spacecraft can approach 25%.Cables are not modeled in detail because no one cared about the “mid frequency” range until a need for better large precision structure models was identified.  Mission performance is driven by on-orbit dynamics: better models are required.The program was directed to finding a solution to an Air Force need, not to develop an understanding of the fundamental mechanics of cable behavior.Applied research

shapes.name: Title 1
shapes.text: The Significance of Cable Modelling

shapes.name: Content Placeholder 2
shapes.text: Electrical cables mounted on space structures can influence the structural dynamics. The effects of cables on spacecraft dynamics is not documented in the industry. Cables not included in models can impact controller performance and robustness, impact isolation system requirements and increase program risk.

shapes.name: TextBox 4
shapes.text: Model errors are determined late in the flight program (i.e., when cables exist). Is there time for controller tuning? The worst time to determine that the controller is miss-tuned is when the satellite is on-station.

shapes.name: Title 1
shapes.text: The What of theCable Effects Study / Focus Restrictions

shapes.name: Content Placeholder 2
shapes.text: Only studied small-to-moderate conductor count twisted pair cable bundles.  Not coaxial, ribbon cables, twisted pair in wire or polymer braided sleeving.Concerned with low-level vibration problem (i.e., when the spacecraft is on-station), not launch vibration or shock conditions.Cables with bends and connectors excluded from study.

shapes.name: Title 1
shapes.text: The How of the Cable Effects Study

shapes.name: Content Placeholder 2
shapes.text: Cable models are implemented using Nastran standard elements. Well integrated with standard analysis toolsLinear beam elements are appropriate, using composite properties and general formulation.Measurements showed that cable models must include shear: a Bernoulli-Euler beam formulation cannot predict cable dynamicsEquivalent cable properties in the Nastran deck are obtained through experiment and parameter estimationThe cable-to-structure model uses linear spring elements (PBUSH)Spring properties were identified through experiment Validation experiments used throughout the program for cable parameter estimation and modeling techniquesDemonstration experiment to verify methodsValidation and verification – it was a research program
